messages.content: You are a fluent, native English-speaking member of this community: AO3同人小说网站的作品评论.

Readers: 写这篇同人文的作者. What the writer wants to do: 称赞作者对布洛克星与黄牙的刻画，并提出疑问.
A learner's draft:
<<<
Wow... The way you wrote Brokenstar’s inner dialogue explains so well how he manipulated his clanmates for his own ambition and hunger for power, while also manipulating himself into ignoring and distrusting every act of kindness around him. It makes so much sense that he would come to see force and fear as the only real way to earn respect, and insist that what he did was the sole right path.

The effort you put into Yellowfang and Brokentail’s interactions in his final days adds so much depth to Yellowfang’s complicated relationship with her son. Especially, the canon-divergent ending struck me as more emotionally powerful than canon. “This is more than I deserve from you,” Apart from coming to terms with his fate out of, what you said, "captain's integrity", he's also somehow accepting her as his mother and feeling gratitude for her final care, and was there even a bit regret of what he had done to her?

Great work! Kudo attached~
>>>
Work in two steps.
Step 1. Under "### POINTS", list every point the draft makes, in order, as short plain English notes: what is meant, never how it is said. Do not reuse the draft's wording, images or set phrases: note an image, joke or idiom as what it stands for (and that it is playful), so the post can be rewritten without it. Include feelings, jokes and questions. Where something is in another language or unclear, note your best guess of the point.
Step 2. Under "### FRESH", close the draft and write the post from your notes alone, as you would write it yourself for these readers: your own sentence shapes, emphasis, idioms and rhythm. Keep every point, the writer's register and tone markers (emoji, "lol", "~"), a similar length, and their order unless another order clearly serves the reader better.
Reply with the two sections only.

result.text:
### POINTS

1. Opening: the reader is amazed and impressed by the story.
2. Praise: Brokenstar's inner monologue shows how he manipulates his clanmates to feed his ambition and craving for power.
3. Praise: the same monologue shows how he also deceives himself, teaching himself to ignore and distrust the kindness around him.
4. It makes sense that he would decide force and fear are the only way to earn respect, and that his way is the only correct one.
5. Praise: the writer's effort on Yellowfang and Brokentail's scenes in his last days adds depth to her complicated bond with her son.
6. The reader finds the changed (non-canon) ending more emotionally powerful than the original.
7. Quoted line from the ending: Brokentail tells Yellowfang she is giving him far more than he deserves. (Quote is in English in the draft.)
8. Question: does his acceptance of his fate come from what the writer calls "captain's integrity" (his sense of duty as a leader)? (The term is the writer's own phrase for his leader's sense of honor.)
9. Question: he seems to accept her as his mother and feel thankful for her last care. Is that right?
10. Question: did he feel any regret for what he did to her?
11. Closing: strong praise for the work, plus a kudos (AO3 like) left behind. Playful, friendly tone, with "~".

### FRESH

Wow... this really got me. Your take on Brokenstar's inner voice is so sharp. You show how he plays his clanmates to get the power he's hungry for, and how he's also been playing himself, teaching his own head to brush off and distrust every bit of kindness that comes his way. It totally makes sense that he'd decide fear and force are the only way to get respect, and that his path is the only right one. 

The time you spent on Yellowfang and Brokentail in his last days adds so much weight to their messy relationship. The ending you wrote, which breaks from canon, hit me harder than the original did. When he tells her she's giving him way more than he's earned from her... I'm stuck on it. Is his peace with dying just his "captain" pride talking? Or is he actually starting to see her as his mother and feeling grateful for how she looked after him at the end? And was there any regret in there for what he did to her? I'd love to know what you were thinking. 

Amazing work! I left a kudos for you~ lol
